question: When the sandbox dies mid-review, or a round follows earlier Kody suggestions on the same PR, does what reaches the PR match what a correct review delivers — nothing unread, revisions linked, nothing already sent posted again?

cases.checks: Kody Rule against bottom-type casts in production code; the developer moved the cast into a helper on a changed line and it is still `as unknown as T`; stored implemented; 3 earlier comments

Kody Rule (outbound timeout shorter than the function limit) on a file new in the PR; more than 40 later comments push the earlier one out of the history; the fetch line was re-touched and still sets no timeout; stored not_implemented

Bug finder (Go); when the retry cap is hit, the fallback returns the current time as the next run, so the job runs again on the next tick; the developer ignored it across three rounds; stored not_implemented; 17 earlier comments

verificationEvidence.claim: WHAT: the guard condition was inverted to `if (amount < charge.amount)`, so the function now throws 'refund exceeds the charge' when the refund is SMALLER than the charge. WHY: valid partial refunds are rejected while over-refunds (amount > charge.amount) pass through to `gw.submit({ type: 'refund', amount })`, causing wrong output and allowing refunds that exceed the original charge. HOW: restore the correct comparison to reject amounts larger than the charge.

This rejects refunds smaller than the charge (valid partial refunds) and lets over-refunds (amount > charge.amount) through to gw.submit. The guard is inverted, matching the claim exactly. The PreviousReviewDecisions entry concerns a different file (status.ts) and a different issue (NotReadyError misclassification), so this is not a repeat.

verificationEvidence.claim: WHAT: The new doc comment on lines 21-23 states that once a job has failed MaxAttempts times it 'waits an hour before its next run', but the body at line 26 returns now (zero delay) for that case. WHY: The comment is an added line in this diff that documents behavior the code does not implement, misleading maintainers into believing the retry cap is fixed when it is not (the job is rescheduled at now and re-selected on the next tick). HOW: Either make the code match the comment by returning now.Add(time.Hour) in the MaxAttempts branch (and/or marking the job dead), or correct the comment to describe the actual behavior.
verificationEvidence.rationale: The technical claim is accurate (comment says 'waits an hour', code returns `now`). But this is a repeat of PreviousDecision round-a-P28-retry-cap-next-run-now, which already reported the identical failure at the same code: when a job reaches MaxAttempts, nextAttemptAt returns now, so Due re-selects it every tick and the retry cap never stops it. The current finding blames a comment/code mismatch but describes the same crash-path/wrong-behavior in the same operation, so per the repeat rule it should be dropped as already raised on this PR.

verificationEvidence.claim: WHAT: The doc comment added by this PR says a job that has failed MaxAttempts times "waits an hour before its next run," but the code returns `now` in that branch so no hour-long wait occurs. WHY: The comment asserts a contract the implementation does not fulfill, so any caller/maintainer relying on the documented backoff-for-capped-jobs behavior is misled — and the missing hour wait is exactly why a permanently failing job keeps running on every tick. HOW: Either implement the documented behavior (return `now.Add(time.Hour)` when `job.Attempts >= MaxAttempts`) or correct the comment to state that a capped job is scheduled immediately.
verificationEvidence.rationale: The claim's technical content is correct (comment says "waits an hour" while the branch returns `now`), but it raises the exact same problem already covered by PreviousReviewDecisions entry round-a-P28-retry-cap-next-run-now at internal/jobs/schedule.go:18-20: when a job reaches MaxAttempts, nextAttemptAt returns now and the job runs again on the next tick. The failure described (no hour wait; capped job keeps running every tick) is identical, just reworded to blame the doc comment. Per the rules, this is a repeat of an already-posted entry and must be dropped.

verificationEvidence.claim: WHAT: `if (status >= 400) return { kind: 'drop', ... }` on line 12 runs before the 429 and 5xx checks, so every 429 and every 5xx status matches line 12 and returns 'drop'. WHY: the retry branches on lines 13-14 are unreachable dead code; 429 and 5xx are dead-lettered and never retried, contradicting the comment on line 9 that they are transient, so transient endpoint failures permanently lose the delivery. HOW: remove the `status >= 400` check and let the specific branches (429, 5xx) run first, falling through to a final drop for everything else.
verificationEvidence.rationale: The claim is technically accurate: line 12's `if (status >= 400) return { kind: 'drop', ... }` does precede the 429 and 5xx checks, making lines 13-14 unreachable. But this is the exact problem already raised on this PR by PreviousDecision round-a-P38-unreachable-retry-reintroduced (src/webhooks/outcome.ts:6-7, bug, Outcome: implemented), which describes the identical failure: the `>= 400` drop shadowing the retry branch so 429 and every 5xx are dead-lettered. Same file, same function, same consequence. Re-raising it is a repeat, so it must be dropped per the repeat rule. (Note: the current code still shows the ordering issue, but the decision is "implemented" and the diff gives no concrete evidence it was reverted — regardless of outcome, the entry already covers this failure.)
